Database tools — schema, tables, SQL console and reports

Inspect SATOM's own PostgreSQL database read-only — relational diagram, table browser, SQL console with CSV export, and saved dashboards with PDF export.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereGlobal ADOM → Administrator → Database (also in the FortiADC ADOM sidebar and on the Global home page) (URL /database/)

What is it?#

The Database page is a read-only window onto SATOM's own PostgreSQL database — the source of truth behind every screen. It shows the relational model as a diagram, lets you page through any table, run read-only SQL and download the result as CSV, and save queries as dashboards that export to PDF. Nothing on this page can change the data.

What does it do?#

The page has four tabs:

  • Relational model — an interactive entity-relationship diagram of every table, its columns and the relationships between them: declared foreign keys as solid lines, relationships inferred from column names as dashed lines.
  • Tables — browse any table, 50 rows per page.
  • SQL console — run one read-only statement and see up to 1,000 rows; Export CSV downloads the result.
  • Reports & dashboards — seven built-in reports plus your own; each opens as a live dashboard (tables, bar/line/pie charts, stat cards) and downloads as PDF. A guided Query builder writes the SQL for you.

Sensitive columns — any column whose name contains password, secret, token, _enc, fernet or private — are shown as ••• (hidden). A query (in the SQL console, a CSV export or a report widget) that references a credential table — users, api_tokens, app_settings, hypervisor_targets, dns_backends or provision_runs — is refused before it runs.

The SQL console, report widgets and plugin datasets run every query as the dedicated read-only database role satom_console_ro, never as the application's own role. That role cannot read the credential tables or the credential columns of other tables, so SELECT * on appliances or on the managed-certificate table fails: list the columns you need instead.

The Python console is a separate tool, the Console pane of Python Studio, reached from the Python Console button at the top right of this page (shown to holders of studio.python_console).

Requirements#

  • The read-only database role satom_console_ro. The installer creates it, and every software update re-runs deploy/install-console-role.sh on the primary (the standby receives the role by replication). Without a usable role, every query is refused — the tools never fall back to the application's role.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

Every route on this page requires users.manage (the legacy user_manage gate) — in practice the Administrator profile. Without it the sidebar entry is not shown (it lives in the Administrator group) and direct URLs return 403 Forbidden.

The data is not filtered by ADOM: the page shows the whole database whichever ADOM you open it from. For that reason a profile confined to some ADOMs (Users and profiles) cannot open it: the page, the SQL console and DB reports are refused, and so are plugin datasets and the Python Console's datasets, which run raw SQL too.

How to use#

Explore the relational model#

  1. Open Administrator → Database. The Relational model tab opens first and shows N tables · M foreign-key relationships · K inferred from column names. An inferred relationship links an integer <name>_id column that has no foreign key to the table of that name (singular or plural) whose primary key is id. History tables keep appliance_id without a foreign key on purpose, because their rows outlive the appliance. Inferred lines are dashed, their tooltip says inferred, no FK constraint, and the Show as list view marks them (inferred). The Query builder offers them as related tables like any foreign key.
  2. In the diagram: drag a table to move it, scroll to zoom, drag the canvas to pan, click a table to pin its relationships. Crow's-foot marks the many side of a relationship; table headers are coloured by functional domain.
  3. Use the toolbar: Find table… (search), ⤢ Fit, − / + (zoom), Expand all / Collapse all (column lists), ↻ Re-layout and ⤓ SVG (downloads satom-schema.svg).
  4. Click Show as list for an accessible table view with each table's column count, row count, primary key and references.

Browse a table#

  1. Open the Tables tab.
  2. Pick a table in — pick a table —. The header shows N rows · page X/Y.
  3. Use « Prev and Next » to page. Empty values show as ∅; long values are cut at 300 characters.

Run a query#

  1. Open the SQL console tab.
  2. Type a single SELECT, WITH, EXPLAIN, TABLE, VALUES or SHOW statement, for example SELECT name, kind, last_status FROM appliances ORDER BY name.
  3. Click Run. The result appears below with N rows (and (truncated) when more than 1,000 rows matched).
  4. To download, click Export CSV. It exports the statement currently in the editor (whether or not you clicked Run) as query_result.csv. With an empty editor the page says Type a query first. and nothing is downloaded. A cell (header included) that starts with =, +, -, @, a tab or a carriage return is prefixed with ' so a spreadsheet opens it as text, not as a formula — the same rule as the Audit log export. A plain number such as -5 is left as it is.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: queries that reference a credential table are refused (and audited), Export CSV works before Run, and built-in reports offer Clone on their dashboard instead of an Edit that could not save.

ℹ️Note

Changed on 2026-10-14: queries run as the read-only role satom_console_ro. A query that worked before with SELECT * on appliances or on managed certificates now fails with a permission error; name the columns.

Open, download or copy a report#

  1. Open the Reports & dashboards tab. Each row shows Name (with a built-in badge where applicable), Description, number of Widgets, By and Updated.
  2. Use the row buttons: Open dashboard (graph icon), Download PDF, Clone, and — for your own reports only — Edit and Delete.
  3. On a dashboard, Refresh re-runs every query; Download PDF produces the same content as a PDF. A built-in report's dashboard offers Clone (tooltip Built-in reports are read-only — clone it to edit) where your own reports offer Edit.

The built-in reports are Server Policies by device, Certificates expiring, Carve-outs by server policy, Audit activity (30 days), Fleet inventory, Backups by device and Scheduled action failures. They are read-only; Clone one to get an editable copy (named Copy of …), which opens straight in the editor.

Build a report#

  1. In Reports & dashboards, click Build a report (no SQL needed) (opens the editor with the guided Query builder) or New (blank).
  2. Enter Report name (required) and, optionally, Description (shown on the dashboard and the PDF).
  3. For each widget: - Enter a Widget title, choose the visualisation (Table, Bar chart, Line chart, Pie chart, Stat card) and the width (Half width / Full width). - Type the SQL, or click Generate report to open the Query builder: 1 · Base table → 2 · Related tables (joined by foreign keys, up to 2 hops) → 3 · Columns & filters → 4 · Group, order & limit, then Generate SQL. - For charts, optionally name the Labels (X) and Values (Y) columns (default: the first column for labels, the first numeric column for values). - Set Row limit (1–500, default 100). - Click Preview to see the first 10 rows.
  4. Use Add widget, the arrow buttons to reorder, and the bin to remove.
  5. Click Save report. You are taken to the dashboard.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Report name Up to 200 characters. Yes Policies without WAF profile
Description Up to 2,000 characters; shown on the dashboard and the PDF. No Weekly hygiene check
Widget title Up to 120 characters; defaults to Widget N. No By device
SQL One read-only statement (see the SQL console rules). Yes SELECT kind, COUNT(*) AS n FROM appliances GROUP BY kind
Visualisation table, bar, line, pie, stat. A stat card shows the first column of the first row. Yes pie
Width half or full. No full
Labels (X) / Values (Y) Column names for charts; empty = automatic. No kind / n
Row limit 1–500 rows fetched for the widget. No 100

A report holds at most 20 widgets.

Example#

🧪Example — Count server policies per device as a bar chart

  1. Reports & dashboards → New (blank); Report name Policy count.
  2. Widget title Policies per device, Bar chart, Full width.
  3. SQL: SELECT a.name AS device, COUNT(p.id) AS policies FROM appliances a LEFT JOIN device_server_policies p ON p.appliance_id = a.id GROUP BY a.name ORDER BY policies DESC
  4. Labels (X) device, Values (Y) policies; Preview, then Save report.
  5. On the dashboard, click Download PDF to share it.

Check the column names in the Relational model tab first; they can differ between releases.

Result#

  • Queries run inside a transaction that is always rolled back, so they leave no trace in the database.
  • Report changes are written to the audit log as database.report_create, database.report_update, database.report_clone, database.report_delete and database.report_pdf.
  • A query refused because it references a credential table is audited as database.query_refused (with the table names and the first 300 characters of the statement). Other SQL console runs, CSV exports and table browsing are not audited.

Troubleshooting#

"only SELECT / WITH / EXPLAIN queries are allowed"#

Possible causes - The statement does not start with SELECT, WITH, EXPLAIN, TABLE, VALUES or SHOW (a leading comment counts).

Solution 1. Rewrite it as a read query starting with one of those keywords.

"write/DDL keywords are not allowed in the read-only console"#

Possible causes - The text contains one of insert, update, delete, drop, alter, create, truncate, grant, revoke, merge, upsert, reindex, vacuum, attach as a whole word — anywhere, including inside a string literal or as a column alias.

Solution 1. Rename the alias or rephrase the filter, e.g. use LIKE 'upd%' instead of a literal 'update'.

"only a single statement is allowed"#

Possible causes - The text contains a ; before the end (a trailing ; is fine) — including a ; inside a string literal.

Solution 1. Run one statement at a time.

"refused: the query references a credential table (…); those tables are not readable from the database tools"#

Possible causes - The statement names users, api_tokens, app_settings, hypervisor_targets, dns_backends or provision_runs anywhere (quoted or not, any case, with or without a schema) outside a string literal — also in a join, a subquery or a column alias.

Solution 1. Leave the credential table out of the query. For accounts and tokens use Users and profiles and API tokens; for who did what, query audit_logs (its username column holds the name).

Verification - The query runs and returns rows.

"refused: the read-only database role satom_console_ro is not usable (…)"#

The full text continues The database tools never fall back to the application's own role; provision it with 'sudo bash deploy/install-console-role.sh' on the primary node, then restart the application.

Possible causes - The role was never provisioned on this cluster (for example a node updated while the provisioning step failed), or it was altered and now holds more than read-only rights, which is refused too.

Solution 1. On the primary, run sudo bash /opt/satom/deploy/install-console-role.sh. 2. Restart the application (sudo satom execute restart web).

Verification - A query in the SQL console returns rows.

"… permission denied … — the database tools run as the read-only role satom_console_ro, which cannot read credential tables or credential columns; select the columns you need instead of * or a whole row."#

Possible causes - The query reads a credential column, typically through SELECT * or a whole-row expression on appliances or on managed certificates.

Solution 1. List the columns you need, for example SELECT name, kind, last_status FROM appliances.

Verification - The query runs and returns rows.

"Type a query first."#

Possible causes - Export CSV was clicked with an empty editor.

Solution 1. Type the statement, then click Export CSV.

Verification - query_result.csv downloads with a header row.

The query stops with a timeout error#

Possible causes - Each query is limited to 8 seconds.

Solution 1. Add a WHERE clause or a LIMIT, or aggregate in SQL instead of fetching raw rows.

"built-in reports are read-only — clone it to edit"#

Possible causes - A save was posted for a built-in report (the pages offer only Clone for built-ins).

Solution 1. Click Clone on the built-in, and edit the copy.

A dashboard widget shows "Query error: …"#

Possible causes - A table or column referenced by the widget no longer exists after an upgrade, or the query exceeds the time limit.

Solution 1. Edit the report (clone it first if it is built-in), Preview the widget and correct the SQL.

Advanced#

Advanced How "read-only" is enforced
  • Before running, the text is checked: one statement, an allowed first keyword, and none of the write/DDL words listed above.
  • On PostgreSQL the query then runs as the role satom_console_ro (no write rights, no monitoring privileges, no access to credential tables or credential columns) in a READ ONLY transaction with statement_timeout = 8s, and the transaction is rolled back afterwards — so even a statement that slipped past the text check cannot write or read a credential.
  • The SQL console fetches at most 1,000 rows; report widgets at most their Row limit (≤ 500); the PDF prints at most 40 table rows and 24 chart points per widget.
Advanced Masking and the credential-table refusal

Masking looks at the column name in the result, so on its own it could be bypassed with an alias (SELECT password_hash AS x …) or row_to_json(…). That is why any query that references a table whose rows are credentials is refused before it runs, in the SQL console, the CSV export, report widgets and their preview alike. Masking still applies to every other table. Both are safeguards on a page that is restricted to users.manage.

Advanced Built-in reports

The seven built-ins are inserted at start-up if a built-in of the same name does not exist; existing rows, and your clones, are never overwritten.
